takeaway: Quadratus femoris inserts below the greater trochanter; the other four hang on the trochanter itself.

question.text: Which of the following muscles does not insert into the greater trochanter of the femur?

lines.text: Picture the greater trochanter as a tree stump on the outer side of the upper femur.
Four muscles tie their ropes right onto it: piriformis, superior gemellus, inferior gemellus and gluteus minimus.
Gluteus medius and obturator internus attach there too, and gluteus medius and minimus are hip abductors.
Quadratus femoris is a short external rotator of the hip, just like the others.
lines.say: Quadratus femoris is a short external rotator of the hip, just like the others. (laugh)

lines.text: But look where it ties on: lower down, on a ridge below the stump, not on the trochanter itself.
So the muscle that does not insert into the greater trochanter is quadratus femoris.
